preferences: Prefer GPT-6 Astra (gpt-6-astra) for 3D modelling, including mesh and geometry creation, CAD, and 3D scene composition. This is a routing preference, not a benchmark claim; choose an eligible Astra candidate subject to task constraints and launch gates.

For bounded routine source collection, mechanical edits, repetitive migrations, and focused checks with explicit acceptance criteria, prefer an eligible gpt-6-luna at max. Keep novel architecture, critical behavior decisions, and final integration judgment with a suitably capable owner. When choosing a stronger candidate for that routine work, name the specific uncertainty or failure consequence that makes Luna insufficient; project importance or write access alone is not that reason. This is a task-routing preference, not a benchmark or measured quota-cost claim.

Effort labels compare budgets within the same model; max on a smaller model does not by itself make that candidate a premium or exceptional choice across models. Apply maximum-effort proportionality against eligible lower efforts of that same model, and judge cross-model task fit separately.

For Claude launches, consider Sonnet 5.5 medium for well-specified coding and multistep tool work, high for harder or longer tasks, and low for short latency-sensitive requests. Consider Haiku 5.5 medium for bounded subagent work, summarization, extraction, classification, and routine coding; use high for longer tasks or stricter instruction following. Prefer Sonnet over Haiku for complex agentic coding. This task-fit guidance comes from Anthropic, not a cross-provider benchmark ranking; apply exact-effort evidence, principal preferences, and launch gates.

For Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, consider xhigh or max only with task-relevant evidence of improvement over lower effort. Haiku low may skip searches or checks in long agent prompts; use medium or high when those checks determine acceptance. API token prices do not establish subscription-quota savings.

methodology.reasoning: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index divided by 100 at the exact effort; the cell names its index version, and different versions are not comparable.
methodology.implementation: CursorBench 4.0 resolved-task rate at the exact effort; candidates without a CursorBench row keep their DeepSWE v1.1 rate, a separate scale that runs about 30 points higher for the same model.
methodology.task-cost: DeepSWE average task cost only when the benchmark names the exact model and effort. An equivalent launch tuple may transfer across harnesses; effort-level proxies remain unknown.
methodology.agentic: AA-Briefcase v1.1 Elo at the exact effort, mapped as (Elo - 500) / 2000.
methodology.ui: Percentile of the dated Arena WebDev rank at the exact effort.
methodology.spatial-3d: Percentile of the dated Design Arena 3D rank at the exact effort.
methodology.conservative: A documented lower estimate reflecting effort or harness transfer and evidence confidence; it is the value used for routing.
methodology.boundary: Public research only. No local model evaluation contributes capability scores; missing direct evidence remains unknown or is labeled as a proxy on the capability evidence itself.
methodology.scale: Every known cell names its benchmark and version in scale. Scores on different scales are not comparable; the brief letters each scale where a column mixes them.
